translations.text: And Moab spurned Israel after the death of Ahab.

And Ahaziah went up onto the lattice of his upper chamber, which was in Samaria, and he fell down and became sick. And he sent messengers to Ekron and said to them: "Go and inquire for me of Baal, the troublesome fly, the god of the Ekronites, whether I shall recover from this sickness of mine." And they went to inquire.

And the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah and said to him: "Arise and go to meet the messengers of Ahaziah, king of Israel, who is in Samaria, and speak to them and say to them: 'Is it because there is no God or prophet in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal, the troublesome fly, the god of Ekron?'
It is not so. Therefore thus says the Lord: 'The bed you have gone up on, you shall not come down from it, but on it you shall surely die.'" And Elijah went and said this to them.
And the messengers returned to Ahaziah, and he said to them: "What is it, that you have come back?"

And they said to him: "A man came up and met us, and he said to us: 'Go, return to the king who sent you, and say to him: Thus says the Lord: Is it because there is no God or prophet in Israel that you send to inquire of Baal, the troublesome fly, the god of the Ekronites? It is not so. Therefore thus says the Lord: The bed you have gone up on, you shall not come down from it, but you shall surely die, because you have done evil before me to provoke me to anger. Behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Ahab, and I will kindle a fire after him, and I will destroy from Ahab every one who urinates against the wall, both the bound and the one left in Israel.'"
The king said to them: "What was the appearance of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
And they said: "A hairy man, with a leather belt girded around his loins." And Ahaziah said: "This is Elijah the Tishbite."

And Ahaziah sent to Elijah a captain of fifty and his fifty men with him, and they went to him; and he was sitting on the top of the mountain. And the captain of fifty went up to him, and his fifty with him, and they came to the man of God. The captain of fifty spoke to him and said: "Man of God, thus says the king: Come down quickly."

Elijah answered the captain of fifty and said to him: "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." And fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.
And the king again sent to him another captain of fifty and his fifty. And they went up to him, and the captain of fifty spoke and said to him: "Man of God, thus says the king: Come down."
Elijah answered and said to him: "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty with you." And fire came down and consumed him and his fifty with him.

And the king again sent a third captain of fifty, and he bowed down on his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him, and spoke and said to him: "Man of God, let my life and the lives of these fifty, your servants, be honored in your sight,
for behold, fire came down from heaven and consumed the two captains of fifty and the fifty of each of them. And now let the life of your servants be precious in your sight."
The angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah and said to him: "Go down with them and do not be afraid of them." So Elijah got up, went down, and went with them to the king.

Elijah spoke to the king and said: "This is what the Lord says: You sent messengers to ask Baal, the fly-god of the Ekronites, for an answer. Was there no God or prophet in Israel to ask for a word? Because of this, you will not come down from the bed you have gone up onto. You will surely die on it."
And Ahaziah died, as the Lord had said through Elijah. Joram, Ahaziah's brother, became king in his place, because he had no son.
As for the rest of the acts of Ahaziah and everything he did, look, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Joram son of Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria for twelve years. Joram son of Ahab became king in Samaria in the first year of Joram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
Joram son of Ahab did evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as his father, his brothers and his mother had done.
He removed the sacred pillars his father had made and smashed them. But he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made all Israel sin, and he did not turn away from them.
And the Lord was angry and furious with him and with the house of Ahab.
When Elijah was about to be taken up in a whirlwind (literally, "with a shaking"), as if into heaven, Elijah and Elisha set out from Gilgal.
Elijah said to Elisha: "Stay here, because the Lord has sent me as far as Bethel." Elisha said: "As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So they came to Bethel.

The sons of the prophets who were at Bethel came out to meet him. They said to Elisha: "Do you know that the Lord is taking your master away from you today?" Elisha said to them: "I know it too. Be quiet."
Elijah said to Elisha: "Stay here, because the Lord has sent me to Jericho." Elisha said: "As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.
The sons of the prophets at Jericho came up to Elisha and said to him: "Do you know that the Lord is taking your master away from you today?" Elisha said to them: "I know it too. Be quiet."
Elijah said to Elisha: "Stay here, because the Lord has sent me as far as the Jordan." Elisha said: "As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So the two of them went on.
Fifty men from the sons of the prophets came and stood facing them at a distance, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.
Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the water with it. The water divided to one side and the other, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
After they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha: "Ask what I should do for you before I am taken up from you." Elisha said: "Let the spirit that is on you be on me twice over."
Elijah said to him: "You have asked for something hard. But if you see me as I am taken up from you, it will be yours. If you do not see me, it will not be."

As they were walking along and talking, suddenly there were chariots of fire and horses of fire, and they separated the two of them from each other. And Elijah was taken up in a whirlwind (literally, "with a shaking"), as if into heaven.
And Elisha was watching, and he cried out and said: "Father, father, chariot of Israel and its horseman!" And he saw him no more. And Elisha took hold of his own garments and tore them in two.
And Elisha took up the mantle of Elijah, which had fallen upon him.

And he struck the waters with it, and they did not part. And Elisha said: "Where is the Lord, the God of Elijah, aphpho?" And so he struck the waters a second time, and the waters were divided, and he crossed over on dry ground.

The sons of the prophets who were at Jericho, opposite him, saw Elisha as he was coming back, and they said: "The spirit of Elijah has come to rest upon Elisha." And they came out to meet him and bowed down to him to the ground.

And they said to him: "Look, there are fifty men with your servants, mighty men. Let them go and search for your master. Perhaps the spirit of the Lord has taken him up and cast him down on one of the mountains or on one of the hills." Elisha said to them: "Do not send them."
And they pressed him until he was ashamed, and he said: "Send them." And they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days and did not find him.
And they turned back and came to him while Elisha was staying in Jericho. Elisha said to them: "Did I not tell you, 'Do not go'?"
And the men of the city said to Elisha: "Look, the site of this city is good, as you yourself, lord, can see, but this water is bad and causes the loss of children."
Elisha said to them: "Bring me a new jar and put salt in it." And they brought it to him.
And he went out to the spring of the water and threw the salt into it and said: "Thus says the Lord: I have healed this water; it shall no longer bring death, nor shall it destroy children any more."
And the water was healed, and has remained so to this day, according to the word of Elisha.

And Elisha went out from there and was going to Bethel. And as he was going up along the road, small boys came out of the city. They threw stones at him and jeered at him, saying: "Go up, baldhead [?], go up!"
And he turned around and saw them and cursed them in the name of the Lord. And two bears came out and tore apart forty-two of the boys.
And he went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
And Joram son of Ahab reigned over Israel for twelve years.
And he did evil before the Lord, but not like his father and his mother. And he removed the pillars that his father had set up.
But he followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray, and did not turn away from them.
And Mesha, king of Moab, was a sheep-breeder, and he paid tribute to the king of Israel: a hundred thousand lambs and a hundred thousand unshorn [?] rams.
And after the death of Ahab, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
And Joram, king of Israel, went out of Samaria on that day, and gave orders and mustered Israel.

And Joram, king of Israel, sent a messenger to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and said: "The king of Moab has broken faith with me. Now, will you come out with me to fight against Moab?" And he said: "I will go out, for as you are, so am I; as your people, so are my people; and as your horses, so are my horses."
And he said: "Tell me, which way shall I take?" And Joram said: "The way of the wilderness, toward Edom."
And they went around on the road for seven days, and no water was found for the army or for their livestock.
The king of Israel said to him, "Alas, for the Lord has given up these three kings, to hand them over into the hands of the king of the Moabites."

And Jehoshaphat king of Judah said, "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here, so that we may inquire of the Lord through him?" And one of the servants of the king of Israel said, "Elisha the son of Shaphat is here, who poured water for washing the hands of Elijah [?]."
And the king of Judah said, "The word is with him." And all three kings went down to him: the king of Israel, the king of Judah and the king of Edom.

And Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother." The king of Israel said to him, "And now the Lord has brought these three kings to hand them over into the hands of the Moabites."
And Elisha said, "As the Lord lives, who has strengthened me before him, if I did not have regard for Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not even look at you or see you.
"But now bring me a musician." And they brought him a musician, and as the music was played, behold, the hand of the Lord came upon him.
And he said, "Thus says the Lord: Dig pools in this valley,
for thus says the Lord: You will not see wind, nor will you see rain, yet that valley will be filled with water, and you and your camp will drink.
And this is a small thing in the eyes of the Lord, and the Lord will give Moab into your hands.
And you will strike down all the choice and strong cities, and you will cut down every fine tree, and you will stop up all the springs of water, and you will ruin every fine piece of land."
And in the morning, at the time of offering the sacrifice, behold, water came flowing down from the outlets of the wilderness of Asudia [?] from Edom, and the land was filled.

And all Moab heard that these kings had come up to fight against them, and they called out everyone who could gird on a belt and bear a sword against them. And they rose early in the morning and stood at their border.
And the sun shone on the water, and Moab [?] saw the water opposite them, for it appeared red like blood.
And they said, "This is the blood of the sword. Those three kings have surely fought fiercely with one another and struck one another down. Now quickly to the spoil, Moab!"
And they went [?] to the camp of Israel, and the Israelites rose up and struck Moab, and they fled before them; and they pursued them and slaughtered Moab.

They overthrew their cities, and on every good portion of land each man threw stones and filled it, and they stopped up every source of the springs with stones, and they cut down every fine tree, and they left not one stone upon another of their walls; and the archers surrounded it and struck it.
And the king of Moab saw that the battle had become too strong for him, and he set out with seven hundred men who drew the sword to break through to the king of Edom, but he could not.

And the king brought his firstborn son, whom he had appointed to reign in his place, and offered him as a sacrifice upon the wall. And there was great remorse among Israel, and they withdrew from there and returned to their own city.

And a woman, one of the wives of the sons of the prophets, cried out to Elisha and said, "Your servant, my husband, has died; and you yourself know that your servant feared the Lord. And behold, the creditor has come and taken both my children to be his slaves."

And Elisha said to her: What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in your house? And she said: There is nothing in the house of your handmaid except one vessel, which holds oil for my anointing.
Elisha said to her: Go and ask for empty vessels for yourself from all your neighbours, many and not few.
And go in, you and your sons, and shut the door, and pour into all those vessels, and it shall not run short.
And the woman went away from him and did so. She and her sons shut the door, and the sons held out the vessels to her, and she poured the oil until the vessels were filled.
She said to her sons: Bring me another vessel. And they said: There is no other. And the oil stopped.
And the woman went and told all this to the man of God. And Elisha said to the woman: Go and give away the oil and pay off your debt, and you and your sons shall live on what is left.
And one day Elisha went to Shunem. There was a rich woman there, and she urged him to eat bread. And many times, whenever he passed that way, he would go in there to eat and drink.
And the woman said to her husband: Look, I know that this man of God is holy, and he is always passing by here.
Let us make him a small upper room and set up a bed, a table and a chair for him there. And when he comes, he can go in there.
And one day Elisha came there, went into the upper room and slept.
And when he woke up, he said to Gehazi his servant: Call the Shunammite woman! And Gehazi called her. She came and stood before him.

Elisha said to his servant: Say to the woman: Look, you have prepared every comfort for us. Now what shall we do for you? Do you have any matter to put to the king, or to the commanders of the army? And she said: I need nothing, for I live among my own people.
Elisha said to Gehazi: What is fitting to do for her? And Gehazi his servant said: This I know: she has no son, and her husband is old.
And Elisha said: Call her! And he called the woman, and she came and stood at the door of the house.
And Elisha said to the woman: At this same season of these days, while you are living, you shall have a child in your arms. And the woman said: No, lord, man of God, do not deceive your handmaid.
And the woman conceived and bore a son at that very season, while she was living, as Elisha had told her.
And the child grew strong. And in the days of harvest the child went out to his father among the reapers.
And he said to his father: My head hurts! And the father ordered one of the servants, saying: Take the child to his mother.
He picked him up and brought him to his mother. And his mother sat him on her knees until noon, and he died.
And she picked him up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut the door and went out.
And she called her husband and said: Send [?] me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so that I may hurry to the man of God and come back.
And her husband said to her: What is it? Why are you going today, since it is neither a new moon nor a Sabbath? And the woman said: Be quiet, all is well.
And they saddled the donkey, and she said to her servant: Lead on and keep going, and do not wait for me to get up on it until I tell you.
And she hurried to the man of God on Mount Carmel. And when Elisha saw the woman coming to him, he said to Gehazi his servant: "Look, there comes that Shunammite woman."
"Run to meet her and say to her: 'Is it well with your husband? Is the child well?'" And she said: "It is well."

And she went to Elisha on the mountain and took hold of his feet. And Gehazi came to push her back. Elisha said: "Let her be, do not speak to her, for she is in pain, and the Lord has hidden it from me and has not told me."
And the woman said: "Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say to you: 'Do not deceive me'?"

And Elisha said to Gehazi: "Tie a belt around your waist, take this staff of mine in your hand, and go. If anyone meets you, do not greet him; and if anyone greets you, do not answer him a word. And lay that staff on the child's face."
And the child's mother said: "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you!" And Elisha got up and followed her.
And Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff on the child's face. But there was no voice and no hearing. And Gehazi came back to meet him and told Elisha: "The child has not risen."
And Elisha went into the house, and there was the child, lying on his bed.
And Elisha went into the house, shut the door, bowed down to the Lord, and prayed to the Lord.

And he went up and lay on the child. He put his mouth on the child's mouth, his eyes on the child's eyes, and his hands on the child's hands, and bent himself over him. And the child's flesh grew warm.
And Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the house, then went up and lay on the child. Seven times he breathed on him, and he strained over him. And the child stirred and opened his eyes.
Elisha called Gehazi and said to him: "Call that Shunammite woman here!" And Gehazi called her. And she came in to him, and Elisha said to her: "Take up your son!"
And the woman went in, fell at his feet, and bowed down to him to the ground. Then she took up her son and went out.

And Elisha returned to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. And Elisha said to his servant: "Put on that big pot and boil some stew for these sons of the prophets."

And one of them went out into the field to gather arioth [herbs]. He found an abandoned vine and gathered from it wild gourds [?], filling his lap [?]. And he brought them and put them into the pot of stew, and he did not know what they were.
And he served it to the men to eat. As they began to eat, they cried out and said: "There is death in this pot, man of God!" And they could not eat it.

And Elisha said: "Bring flour and pour it into this pot!" And they poured it in. And Elisha said to Gehazi his servant: "Serve it to the people, and let them eat!" And nothing in the pot did them any harm.
And a man came from Bethsaida and brought the man of God bread from the first fruits: twenty barley loaves and [?] cakes [?]. And Elisha said: "Give it to the people and let them eat!"

And his servant said: "What would this be for anyone, set before a hundred men?" And Elisha said: "Give it to the people and let them eat, for this is what the Lord says: 'They will eat, and there will be some left over.'"
And he set it before them; they ate, and some was left over, according to the word of the Lord.

And Naaman, the commander of the army of the king of Assyria, was a great man before his lord and held in high honour, for through him the Lord had given deliverance to Assyria. And the man was mighty in strength, and he was a leper.
And lightly armed men had gone out from Assyria and had taken captive a little girl from the land of Israel, and she was with Naaman's wife.
And she said to her mistress: "What if my lord went to the prophet of God in Samaria and entreated him? He would at once cleanse him of that leprosy."
And he went in and told his lord, and said: "Thus and thus said the girl who is from the land of Israel."
And they told this to the king. And the king of Assyria said: "Go, and I will write to the king of Israel." And Naaman took ten talents of silver, six talents of gold, and ten changes of clothing.
And he took the letter to the king of Israel, in which was written thus: "Now, when this letter reaches you, see: I have sent Naaman my servant to you, so that you may cleanse him of his leprosy."

And when the king of Israel had read the letter, he tore his clothes and said: "Am I God, to put to death and to make alive, that he has sent me this man to cleanse him of his leprosy? But know and understand that he is seeking some pretext against me."

And when Elisha, the man of God, heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent to the king of Israel and said: "Why have you torn your clothes? Let Naaman come to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel."
And Naaman came with his chariots and his horses and stood at the door of Elisha's house.
And Elisha sent a messenger to him and said: "Go and wash in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored to you, and you will be clean."
And Naaman became angry and went away, and said: "I thought that he would come out to me, call on the name of the Lord his God, lay his hand on this leprosy, and cleanse me of my leprosy."

"Are not the Abana and the Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than the Jordan and all the waters of Israel? Why should I not go and wash in them and be clean?" And he turned and went away in anger.

And his servants came up and said to him: "My lord, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would it not have been right for you to do it? How much more, then, when he has told you: 'Wash and be clean.'"
And Naaman went down and washed seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of Elisha. And it was restored, and his flesh became like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

And Naaman returned to Elisha, he himself and all his company. And he came and stood near him and said: "Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. And now accept a gift from your servant."
And Elisha said: "As the Lord lives, before whom I have stood [?], I will not accept anything!" And he pressed him to accept it, but he refused.

And Naaman said: "Since you did not wish to take anything, give me leave to load some of these mules with earth from this land. For your servant will not make offerings and sacrifices to foreign gods, but only to the Lord."

"And in this one matter may the Lord forgive your servant: when my lord goes into the house of Rimmon to worship him, he leans his hand on me. And when he goes into the house of Rimmon and bows down and worships, I will worship the Lord my God. May the Lord forgive your servant in this matter."
And Elisha said to Naaman: "Go in peace." And he went away from him, out of the land of Israel.

And Gehazi, his servant, said: "Look, my lord has spared Naaman the Syrian and has taken nothing from him of what he brought him. As the Lord lives, I will run after him and catch up with him and take something from him."
And Gehazi went after Naaman to catch up with him. And when Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he jumped down from his chariot, came to meet him and said: "Is all well?"

And Gehazi said: "All is well. My lord has sent me to you, and he said: 'Look, two young men have just come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Give them a talent of silver and two finished garments.'"

Naaman said: "If that is so, take the talents of silver." And he pressed him, and gave him three talents of silver. He tied them up and put them in two bags, together with two finished garments, and gave them to two of his servants, and they carried them ahead of him.
And when they came to the dark place, he took the things from their hands and put them in the house. And he sent the men away, and they left.
And he went in and stood before his lord. Elisha said to him: "Where have you come from, Gehazi?" And Gehazi said: "Your servant has not gone anywhere, here or there."

Elisha said to him: "Was my heart not with you when the man turned back from his chariots and came to meet you? And now you have taken the silver and the garments, and with it you have acquired gardens and olive groves and vineyards, cattle and sheep, menservants and maidservants.
"Naaman's leprosy shall cling to you and to your descendants forever." And he went out from his presence a leper, white as snow.
And the sons of the prophets said to Elisha: "Look, this place where we live is too small for us.
"Let us go to the Jordan, and let each of us cut a beam, and let us build ourselves a place to live there." And Elisha said: "Go."
And one of them said: "Please come with us too, with your servants." And he said: "I will go."
And he went with them, and they came to the Jordan and cut wood.
And while one of them was cutting a beam, the iron axe-head flew off the handle and fell into the water. The man cried out and said: "Have mercy on me, lord, for it was borrowed!"
And the man of God said: "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place. And Elisha broke off a branch and threw it in right there, and the iron floated up.
And the king of Syria was setting out to make war on Israel. He took counsel with his servants and said: "Let us lie in ambush at a certain place, Phelmon."
And Elisha sent word to the king of Israel and said: "Be careful not to go past those places, for the Syrians are lying in ambush there."
And the king of Israel sent to the place Elisha had told him about, and had it watched, and he kept on guard there, not once or twice but every time.
And the heart of the king of the Assyrians was enraged over this matter. He called his servants and said to them: "Tell me, who is betraying me to the king of Israel?"
And one of the servants said: "No one, my lord the king. It is Elisha, the prophet of Israel. He tells the king of Israel all the words that you speak in the chambers of your bedroom."
And the king said: "Go and see where he is." And they told him: "Look, he is in Dothan."
And the king of Assyria sent horses and chariots and a strong force, and they came by night and surrounded the city.
And Elisha's servant rose early at dawn, and a strong force was surrounding the city, with horses and chariots. And the boy said to him: "Lord, what shall we do?"
And he said to him: "Do not be afraid. Those who are with us are more than those who are with them."

And Elisha prayed, bowed down, and said to the Lord: "Lord, open the eyes of this boy so that he may see!" And the Lord opened the boy's eyes. When the boy looked, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
And they came down to him, and Elisha prayed to the Lord and said: "Strike these people with blindness!" And he struck them with blindness, as Elisha had said.
And Elisha said to them: "This is not the road, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to the man you are looking for." And he went ahead of them and led them to Samaria.
And when they had entered Samaria, Elisha said: "Lord, open the eyes of these men so that they may see!" And the Lord opened their eyes and they looked, and they were in the middle of Samaria.
When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha: "Shall I strike them down, father?"

And he said: "Do not strike them down. Those whom you did not take captive with your sword, would you now destroy them [?]? Instead, set bread and water before them, so that they may eat and go back to their lord."
And he set bread before them, and they ate and drank. He sent them away, and they went back to their lord. And the Assyrians did not come into the land of Israel again.
After this, the son of Hadad, king of Assyria, gathered his whole army, and came and besieged Samaria.
And there was a great famine in Samaria. They besieged it until a donkey's head sold for eighty shekels of silver, and four kabs of dove's dung for five shekels of silver.
And Joram, king of Israel, was walking on the wall, and a woman cried out to him and said: "Save me, my lord the king!"
And he said: "If the Lord does not save you, where could I save you from? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?"
The king said to her: "What is the matter with you?" The woman answered the king: "This woman said to me: 'Come, let us eat your child today, and we will eat this child of mine tomorrow.'"
"So we boiled my child and ate him. And the next day I said to her: 'Now bring your child too, and let us eat him.' But she hid her child."
And it happened that when the king heard what the woman said, he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth, and he was walking on the walls. When the people saw the sackcloth he wore against his body,
he said: "May God do so and so to me, and more besides, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat stays on him today."

Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king sent a man to him. Before the messenger reached him, Elisha said to the elders: "Do you know that this son of a murderer has sent someone to cut off my head? Watch, and when he comes in, hold the door shut against him and press him in it, for look, the sound of his master's feet is behind him."
While he was still speaking to them, the messenger reached them and said: "Look, this evil is from the Lord. Why should we keep pleading with the Lord?"
Elisha said: "Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: Tomorrow at this hour, a single measure of fine flour will be found for one shekel at the gates of Samaria."

The messenger on whose hand the king leaned answered Elisha and said: "Even if the Lord made floodgates in the heavens, could this thing happen?" Elisha said to him: "Look, you will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
There were four men with leprosy outside the gate of the city. One said to his companion: "Why should we sit here and die?
If we go into this city, we will die, because there is famine in it. So now let us go over to the camp of the Syrians. If they spare our lives, we will live, and if they kill us, we will die."
They got up at first light, at dawn, and reached the camp of the Syrians. They entered one side of their camp, and no one was there,

for God had made the camp of the Syrians hear the sound of chariots, the noise of horses, and the sound of a mighty army. And each man said to his brother: "Look, the king of Israel has hired [?] two kings against us: the king of the Egyptians
So they fled by night and left their tents, their mounts, and their donkeys in the camp. They got up and fled to save nothing but their own lives.

Those men [?], worn down by hunger, went into one tent. They ate and drank, took silver, gold, and clothing from it, and went and hid them. Then they came back, went into another tent, took things from there as well, and hid them.

Then the lepers said to one another: "What we are doing is not right. This is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent and waiting for the light of dawn. We will be found guilty of wrongdoing. So now let us go and tell this to the king's household."

They went and stood at the gate of the city, crying out. They told them: "We went into the camp of the Syrians, and there was no one there, not even the sound of a human voice. There were only horses and donkeys tied up, and their tents left standing as they were pitched."
The gatekeepers stood and cried out, and they reported it to the king's household.

The king got up, called his servants, and said to them: "I will tell you what the Syrians have done to us. They knew that we are starving, so they left the camp and hid from us outside, saying: 'Who knows? They will come out of the city, and we will capture them alive, go into the city, and take it.'"
And one of the servants answered and said: “Let five horses be taken from all the multitude of Israel that remains, and let us send them there, and they will see.”
And they sent two riding horses. And the king of Israel sent men after the king of the Syrians and said: “Go and see!”

And they set out, and the men went after them as far as the Jordan. And behold, all the roads were full of garments and vessels that the Syrians had thrown away in their flight. And the messengers returned and told the king.
And the people went out of the city and plundered the camp of the Syrians. And one measure of fine flour sold for one shekel of silver, according to the word of the Lord that he had spoken to Elisha.

And the king appointed the officer from among the armed men, on whose arm the king leaned, as keeper over the gate. And they trampled him in the crush at the gate, and he died, as the man of God had told him when he came to him as a messenger.

And it happened just as Elisha had told the officer: “Two measures of barley will be had for one shekel, and one measure of fine flour for one shekel, and this will be tomorrow at this same hour at the gate of Samaria.”

The officer answered the man of God and said: “Even if the Lord opened the floodgates of heaven, could this thing happen?” Elisha said to him: “Behold, you will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it.”
And so it happened: the people trampled him in the crush at the gate, and he died.

Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had brought back to life, and said to her: “Arise and go, you and your household, and live as a stranger wherever you can manage, for the Lord has called a famine upon this land, and the famine will be upon this land for seven years.”
And the woman arose with all her household and did as Elisha had said. And she went and lived as a stranger in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
And it came to pass after the seven years of famine that the woman returned from the land of the Philistines and went to appeal to the king for her house and for her land.
And the king was talking with Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, and said: “Tell me all the great things that Elisha has done.”

And it came to pass that as he was telling the king how Elisha had brought the woman's dead son back to life, behold, the woman whose son Elisha had brought back to life came appealing to the king for her house and for her land. And Gehazi said to the king: “My lord king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha brought back to life.”

And the king questioned the woman, and she told him everything. And the king gave her a eunuch and said: “Give back to her everything that is hers, and all the produce of her land from the time she left her land until now.”
And Elisha went to Damascus. And Ben-Hadad, king of Syria, was sick. And they told him, saying: “The man of God has come here.”
And the king said to Hazael: “Take manna in your hands and go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the Lord through him, and say: ‘Will I recover from this sickness of mine?’”

And Hazael went to meet Elisha. He took a gift in his hand, every good thing of Damascus, on forty camels. He came and stood before him and said to him: "Father Elisha! Your son Ben-hadad, king of Syria, has sent me to you, and he said: 'Will I recover from this sickness of mine?'"
Elisha said to him: "Go and tell him: 'You will surely live.' Yet the Lord has shown me that he will surely die."
Hazael stood before Elisha's face in reverence and offered him the gift. And the man of God wept.

Hazael said: "Why are you weeping, my lord?" Elisha said: "I know how much harm you will do to the children of Israel. You will set their strongholds on fire, you will cut down their chosen men with the sword, and you will rip open their pregnant women."

Hazael said: "Who is this servant of yours, a dead dog, that he should do what this great word of yours says?" Elisha said: "The Lord has shown me that you will do this, and that you will reign over Syria."
Hazael left Elisha and went to his lord. His lord said to him: "What did Elisha say?" Hazael said: "He told me: 'He will live.'"
On the next day he took the makma [?] (a cloth), dipped it in water, and covered his face, and he died. And Hazael became king over Syria,
in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel. And Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah.
He was thirty-two years old when he took his seat as king, and he reigned forty years over Jerusalem.
He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife. And he did evil before the Lord.
But the Lord did not wish to destroy Judah, for the sake of his servant David, since he had promised to give a lamp to him and to his son for all days.
In the days of Jehoram, Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah, and they set up a king over themselves.

Jehoram went out from Zion, and all his chariots with him. And early [?] at dawn, while it was still night, they struck Edom, those who surrounded him, and the commanders of his chariots. And the people fled, each to his own tent.
So Edom has been in revolt against the hand of Judah to this day. At that time Libnah also revolted.
The rest of the acts of Jehoram, and all that he did, are written in the book of the days of the king of Judah.
Jehoram slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And his son Ahaziah reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, daughter of Ahab, king of Israel.
He walked in the ways of Ahab and did evil before the Lord, like the house of Ahab, for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
Ahaziah went with Joram son of Ahab to fight against Hazael, king of the Syrians, at Ramoth-gilead. And the Syrians wounded Joram.

And King Joram returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds that the Syrians had given him at Ramoth of Gilead, in his battle against Hazael, king of the Syrians. And Ahaziah, son of Joram, went down to see Joram, son of Ahab, because he was sick in Jezreel.
And Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him: Gird up your loins, take this horn of anointing oil in your hands, and go to Ramoth Gilead.
And you shall go in there and see Jehu there, son of Nimshi, son of Jehoshaphat, and you shall make him rise from among his brothers and bring him into an inner room.
And he took the horn of oil and poured it on his head and said: Thus says the Lord: I have anointed you king over Israel. And open the door and flee, and do not stay any longer.
And the young man, the prophet, went to Ramoth Gilead.

And he went in there, and behold, the commanders of the army were sitting there. And the prophet said: I have a word for you, commander! And Jehu said to him: For whom, or for which of all of us? And he said to him: No, but for you alone, commander.

And Jehu rose, and they went into the room, and he poured the oil on his head, and the prophet said to him: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I have anointed you king over the people of the Lord, over Israel.
And you shall strike down the house of Ahab, your lord, from before you, and you shall avenge the blood of the servants of the Lord on the hands of Jezebel
and on all her house. And destroy every one of the house of Ahab who turns and urinates against the wall, and leave the crushed one in Israel.
to give up the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha, son of Ahijah.
And dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel, and there shall be no one to bury her. When he had said this, the prophet opened the door and fled.

And Jehu came out to the servants of his lord, and they said to him: Is it peace? And Jehu said to them: It is peace. And they said to him: Why did that madman come to you? Jehu said to them: You yourselves know the man and his madness.
And they said to him: It is wrong of you if you do not tell us. And Jehu said to them: He spoke to me thus and thus and said to me: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have anointed you king over Israel.
When they heard this, they hurried, and each of them took his own garment [?] and laid it under Jehu on one of the steps. And all of them blew on a horn trumpet and said: Jehu has become king!
And Jehu, son of Nimshi, son of Jehoshaphat, gathered the people against Joram. And Joram was on guard at Ramoth in Gilead, he himself and all Israel, against Hazael, king of the Syrians.

And King Joram returned from the healing of the wounds that the Syrians had given him in Jezreel, in the battle against Hazael, king of the Syrians. And Jehu said: If your soul is with me, let no fugitive go out of this city to go and tell it in Jezreel.

And Jehu set out and went down to Jezreel. And Joram, king of Israel, was being healed in Jezreel of the wounds he had been given at Ramoth Gilead in the battle against Hazael, king of the Syrians, for he was a brave and strong man. And Ahaziah, king of Judah, had gone down to see Joram.

And the watchman went up onto the tower of Jezreel and saw the dust of Jehu's approach, and he said: "I see some dust." And Joram said: "Bring a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him say: 'Is it peace?'"

And the horseman went to meet them and said to him: "Thus says the king of Israel: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said: "What have you to do with peace? Turn back and stand here." And the horseman stood with them. And the watchman said: "The messenger has reached them and has not come back."

And he sent a second horseman, and he reached them and said to him: "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said to him: "What have you to do with peace? Turn back and stand here." And he too stood with them.
And the watchman reported and said: "Look, the messenger has reached them and has not come back." And the one that Jehu was driving only just arrived [?], for he was driving it furiously.

And Joram said: "Harness those chariots!" And they harnessed them, and both kings mounted the chariots, Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah. They went out to meet Jehu and came upon him at the plot of land of Naboth the Jezreelite.
And when Joram saw Jehu, he said to him: "Is it peace, Jehu?" And Jehu said to him: "What peace? Look, the harlotries of your mother Jezebel and her sorceries have multiplied."
And Joram turned around and fled, and said to Ahaziah: "It is treachery, Ahaziah!"
And Jehu drew his bow and shot Joram between the shoulders and pierced his back, and he collapsed [?] onto his knees.

And Jehu said to Bidkar, his third officer: "Pick him up and throw him into the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite. I remember when the two of us were riding and following Ahab his father, and the Lord laid this fate upon him,
saying: 'I will avenge the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons, which I saw yesterday,' as the Lord said. And I will repay him in the plot of Naboth, according to the word of the Lord."

And when King Ahaziah saw this, he fled by the road of Bethron. And Jehu followed after them and said: "Strike him too!" And they struck him too in the chariot, as he was going up the ascent of Berai, which is at Jobel [Ibleam]. And he fled to Megiddo and died there.
And his servants carried him to Jerusalem and buried him in his own tomb with his fathers in the city of David.
And in the eleventh year of Joram king of Israel, Ahaziah reigned over Judah, and he reigned one year over Israel.
And Jehu came to Jezreel. And when Jezebel heard of it, she painted her eyebrows, adorned her head, and was looking down through the window.
And Jehu entered the city, and [she] said: "Is Zimri alive, the murderer of his lord?"
And Jehu raised his eyes and looked up at the windows and said: "Who are you? Come down to me." And two of her eunuchs looked down at him.
And Jehu said to them: "Throw her down from there to the ground." And they threw her down from there to the ground. Her blood spattered on the walls, and they trampled her with their horses.
And he went in, ate and drank, and said: "See to that accursed woman and bury her, for she is a daughter of kings."
And they went to bury her, and found nothing of her except the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands.

And they told this to Jehu. And Jehu said: That is the word of the Lord which he spoke by the mouth of his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying: In the territory of Jezreel the dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel.
And the corpse of Jezebel shall be like dung in the territory of Naboth's field, so that none of them will say, "This is Jezebel," and no one will say "woe" for her.
Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote to Samaria, to the rulers of Samaria, to the elders, and to Ahab's foster-fathers, and said:
As soon as this letter reaches you, consider: behold, the sons of your lord are with you, and his chariots and horses and fortified cities and his armour are with you —
consider, and choose one of the sons of your lord, set him firmly on his father's throne, and fight for the house of your lord.
They were greatly afraid and said: Behold, these two kings could not stand before him; how then shall we stand before him?

And the elders and the foster-fathers sent from his house and from the city, and they said to Jehu: We are your servants, and whatever you tell us, we will do. We will not set up anyone as king over us, but whatever is pleasing in your sight, that we will do.

And he wrote to them a second time and said: If you are mine, listen to my voice: cut off the heads of the sons of your lord and bring them to me at Jezreel tomorrow at this same hour. The king's sons were seventy, and the great men of the city were bringing them up.
And when the letter reached them, they seized the king's sons and slaughtered all seventy of them, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to him at Jezreel.
They went in, told him, and said: They have brought the heads of the king's sons. And he said: Lay them in two heaps outside the city gate until morning.

And in the morning Jehu went out, stood at the city gate, and said to all the people: You are righteous! Behold, I rose up against my lord and killed him. But look at these: [?] who struck all these down?
For not one of the words of the Lord has fallen to the ground, which the Lord spoke against the house of Ahab. And the Lord has fulfilled everything that he spoke by the mouth of his servant Elijah.
And Jehu struck down all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his rulers, his friends, and his priests, and he left no survivor.
And Jehu arose and went to Samaria. And while he was on his way, at Beth-eked of the shepherds on the road,

Jehu found the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and Jehu said: Who are you? And they said to him: We are the brothers of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the king's sons and the sons of the one in power.
And Jehu said: Seize them alive and slaughter them! And they slaughtered them at Beth-eked, forty-two men, and not one of them was left.

And Jehu went on from there and found Jonadab son of Rechab, and he greeted him with a blessing. And Jehu said to him: Is your heart true, as my heart is toward you? And Jonadab said: It is! And Jehu said: If it is, give me your hand. And he took him up into the chariot.
And he said to him: Come with me and see my vengeance for the Lord. And he took him up into the chariot.
And he went into Samaria and destroyed all who were left of Ahab's house in Samaria, according to the word of the Lord which he had spoken to Elijah.
Jehu gathered all the people and said to them: "Ahab served Baal a little, but I will serve him greatly.

Now bring me all the prophets of Baal, all his servants and all his priests. Let not one of them be missing, for there is a great sacrifice for Baal, and any man who is missing shall die." Jehu did this by deceit, so that he might destroy the servants of Baal.
And Jehu said: "Prepare the sacrifice for Baal." And the herald proclaimed it.
Jehu sent word throughout all Israel, and all the servants of Baal were gathered, and not one was missing. They went into the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled from end to end.
Jehu said to the keepers of the house: "Bring out the vestments."

Then Jehu and Jehonadab the son of Rechab went into the house of Baal, and he said to the servants of Baal: "Search and see that there is no one here with you from among the servants of the Lord, but only you who are the servants of Baal." And they said to them: "There is no one; we are only servants of Baal."

And Jehu went in as if to offer sacrifice and burn incense. Jehu had stationed three hundred and eighty men outside and said: "If any man escapes from among these men whom I am giving into your hands, his life shall be in place of the life of the one who escaped."

And when they had finished the sacrifice, Jehu said to his runners and armed men: "Go in and kill them, and let not one of them escape you." They went in and killed them with the sword and threw them out there, and they went into the house of Baal.
They brought out the pillars of the house of Baal and burned them with fire.
They broke down all the pillars of Baal and demolished the house of Baal, and they made the place into a house of shame, to this day.
Thus Jehu wiped out Baal and his house from Israel.
But from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who led Israel astray, Jehu did not turn away, nor from the golden heifers that were in Bethel and in Dan.

The Lord said to Jehu: "Because you have been zealous before me to do what is upright, and have done to the house of Ahab according to the will of my heart, your descendants to the fourth generation shall sit on the thrones of Israel."
But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the Lord, the God of Israel, with all his heart, and he did not turn away from the sin of Jeroboam, who led Israel astray.
In those days the Lord began to cut down all the territories of Israel. And Hazael struck [?] in all the territories of Israel,
from the Jordan toward the sunrise: all the land of Gilead, of Gad, of Reuben and of Manasseh, from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and Gilead and Bashan.
The rest of the acts of Jehu, all that he did, all his might, and the slaughter that he carried out, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
And Jehu slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria. And Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.
And the days that Jehu reigned over Israel and over Samaria were forty-eight years.
And when Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her sons had been killed, she destroyed all the royal family.

And Jehoshabeath, daughter of King Jehoram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash, the son of Ahaziah her brother, and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being slain. She hid him and his nurse in a bedchamber, away from Athaliah.
He was with her in the house of the Lord for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year Jehoiada the priest sent and brought the commanders, Chorri and Rasim, and brought them into the house of the Lord. He made a covenant with them and made them swear by the name of the Lord, and Jehoiada showed them the king's son.
He commanded them and said to them: "This is what you shall do. Divide yourselves into three parts. One part shall keep guard over the royal house at the doors.
The second part shall guard the gates of the entrances, and the third part the gates behind the runners. So you shall keep guard over the house.
Hold your hands ready. Everyone who goes in among those assigned to guard the house of the Lord, keep careful guard over the house of the Lord.
Surround the king, every man, and take up weapons in your hands. Whoever enters the ranks [Saderoth] shall die!" And he himself was with the king in his coming in and his going out.
The centurions did everything that Jehoiada the priest commanded them. And the men assigned as guards went in, one after another.
Jehoiada the priest went in and gave the centurions the spears and the armor of King David that were in the king's house.
The centurions took the armor in their hands and stood all around, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the temple, and around the altar and the royal house.

Jehoiada the priest gathered all the people in the royal house and presented the king's son to them. He put on him the nezer [crown] and the testimony, anointed him, and made him king. The people clapped their hands and said: "Long live the king!"
Athaliah heard the sound of the people's noise, and she went in among the people, into the house of the Lord.

She looked, and behold, the king was standing by the pillar, according to the custom, and the rulers, the singers of praise, and the trumpeters stood around him, and all the land rejoiced and blew on pipes. Athaliah tore her garment, cried out, and said: "Rebellion! Rebellion!"

Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of thousands and those who had been set over the people, and said to them: "Take her out of the ranks [Saderoth], bring her out behind the house of the commanders, and kill her with the sword! Do not kill her in the house of the Lord. And whoever follows her shall die by the sword!"
They laid hands on her, seized her, and brought her by the way of the horsemen of the royal house, and there they killed her.
Jehoiada the priest made a covenant between the Lord, the king, and the people, that they should be the Lord's people.

All the people went into the house of Baal and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images to small pieces, and they killed Mattan the priest and all the priests of Baal before the sacrifice. And the priest appointed overseers over the house of the Lord.

And Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds, the Carites and the runners, and all the people of the land. And they brought the king down from the house of the Lord and brought him in by the way of the gate of the royal house, and they seated him on the royal thrones.
And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, and they killed Athaliah in the king's house.
Joash was seven years old when he was established as king.
And in the seventh year of Jehu, Joash son of Ahaziah reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
And Joash did what was right before the Lord all the days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
But he did not remove the high places, and there the people sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

Joash said to the priests: "All the silver that is offered to the temple of the Lord as holy offerings, the silver of each man who passes the count, assessed for souls, all the silver that comes into a man's heart to bring into the house of the Lord, —
let the priests take it, each from his own acquaintances, and let them repair the breaches of the house of the Lord everywhere, wherever a breach is found there."
And in the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had not repaired the breaches of the house of the Lord.

King Joash summoned Jehoiada the priest and all the priests and said to them: "Why have you not repaired the breaches of the house of the Lord? Now take no more silver from any of your acquaintances, but give it for the breaches of the house of the Lord."
And the priests agreed not to take silver from the people and not to repair the breaches of the temple of the Lord.
And Jehoiada took a chest and bored a hole in its top, and set it beside the altar of the Lord. And the priests who kept the doors put into it all the silver that was found in the house of the Lord.
And they saw that there was a great deal in the chest. And the chief scribe and the high priest went up and counted the silver that was found in the house of the Lord.
And they gave the silver into the hands of those doing the work on the vessels in the house of the Lord, and they gave it to the carpenters who worked in wood, the builders of the house of the Lord,
and to the carvers and the stonecutters, as payment for timber and hewn stones, to repair the breaches of the house of the Lord. And they gave all the silver for the use of the temple.

And so that they would not make from it, for the house of the Lord, doors of silver, and nails, and basins, and trumpets, and any vessel of gold and silver from what was offered to the house of the Lord,
they gave it instead to those doing the work, to repair the house of the Lord.
And no account of the silver was kept with those into whose hands it was given to pay the workers, for they were faithful.
And the silver offered for sins did not go into the temple of the Lord, but belonged to the priests alone.
At that time Hazael king of Syria went out and fought against Gath and took it. And Hazael set out to go up against Jerusalem.

And Joash, king of Israel, took all the holy things that his fathers Jehoshaphat, Jehoram and Ahaziah, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own holy things too, and all the silver that was found in the treasury of the house of the Lord and in the king's house, and he sent them to Hazael, king of the Syrians. And Hazael went away from Jerusalem.
And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah?
And his servants rose up against him and conspired against him, and they struck him down in the house of Maghon, in the dwellings of Gilead.

And Jozachar son of Jemoth, and Jezeboth his son, who were counted among his servants, struck him and killed him. And they buried him with his fathers in the city of David. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu reigned over Israel and Samaria for seventeen years.
And he did evil before the Lord and followed the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel go astray, and he did not turn away from it.
The Lord was angered with wrath against Israel and gave them into the hands of Hazael, king of the Syrians, and into the hands of the son of Ader, the son of Hazael, all their days.
And Jehoahaz entreated the face of the Lord, and the Lord heard him and saw the affliction of Israel, how the king of the Syrians oppressed them.
And the Lord gave Israel a deliverer, and they escaped from the hands of the Syrians. And the children of Israel settled in their own dwellings, as yesterday and the day before.
But they did not turn away from the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel go astray, but walked in it, and also went to the groves of Samaria.
No people were left to Jehoahaz except only about fifty horsemen, ten chariots and a thousand foot soldiers. The king of the Syrians had destroyed them and made them like dust to be trampled.
And the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and all his might, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Jehoahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in Samaria. And his son reigned in his place.
In the seventeenth year of the reign of Joash, king of Judah, Joash son of Jehoahaz reigned over Israel in Samaria for twelve years.
And he did evil before the Lord and did not turn away from any of the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel go astray, but walked in it.
And the rest of the acts of Joash, all that he did, and all his mighty deeds, and what he did to the king of Judah, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Joash slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat on his throne. And they buried Joash in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
And Elisha fell sick with the illness that he died of. And Joash, king of Israel, came and wept over his face and said, "My father, my father, chariot of Israel and its horseman!"
Elisha said to him, "Take your bow and your arrows!" And he took a bow and arrows.
And Elisha said to the king of Israel, "Take hold of the bow with your hand!" And he took hold of the bow with his hand. And Elisha laid his hands on the king's hands.

And he said: "Open those windows that face east!" And they opened them. And Elisha said: "Shoot!" And he shot. Elisha said: "An arrow of deliverance from the Lord, and an arrow of deliverance against the Syrians. You will strike the Syrians at Aphek and destroy them."
And Elisha said to him: "Take the arrows!" And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel: "Shoot and strike the ground!" And the king struck three times and stopped.
And the man of God was grieved with him and said: "If you had struck five times, you would have overcome the Syrians and destroyed them. But now you will strike the Syrians only three times."
And Elisha died, and they buried him. And Moabite raiders came into the land just as that year was ending.

And it happened that as they were burying a man, they suddenly saw the raiders. And as the raiders were just about to overtake them, they threw the dead man into the grave, among Elisha's bones. And he came to life and stood up on his feet.
And Hazael, king of the Syrians, oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
And the Lord took pity on them and showed them mercy because of the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And the Lord did not want to destroy them, and he did not cast them away from his presence.
And Hazael, king of the Syrians, died, and his son Hadad reigned in his place.

And Joash son of Jehoahaz went and took back from Hadad son of Hazael the lands that Hadad had taken in the war from his father Jehoahaz. And Joash struck Hadad three times, according to the word of the Lord, and he recovered the cities of Israel and everything that had been taken.
In the second year of the reign of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.
Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddin, from Jerusalem.
And he did what was right rather than what was evil before the Lord, though not like his father David. He did everything just as his father Joash had done.
But he did not destroy the high places, and the people went on sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
And it happened that when his kingdom was firmly established in his hand, he killed his servants who had killed the king, his father.

But he did not kill the children of the murderers, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses, where the Lord commanded: "The father shall not die for the children, nor the children for the fathers; each shall die for his own sin."
This Amaziah struck down twelve thousand of Edom in battle at Gemelek. And he took the Rock by war and named it Joktheel, which is its name to this day.
At that time Amaziah sent messengers to Joash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying: "Come, let us meet each other face to face."

Joash, king of Israel, answered Amaziah, king of Judah: "A thistle in Lebanon sent word to a pine of Lebanon, saying: 'Give your daughter to my son as his wife.' And the wild beasts of the forest that were in Lebanon passed over it and trampled the thistle.
You have utterly struck down Edom, and now your heart has become proud. Very well, boast, but stay in your house. Why does your wickedness [?stir you up]? You will fall, and Judah with you."
But Amaziah did not listen. So Jehoash, king of Israel, went out, and he and Amaziah, king of Judah, met face to face at Beth-shemesh of Judea.
And Judah was defeated before Israel, and each man fled to his own home.

And Jehoash, king of Israel, captured Amaziah, king of Judah, son of Josiah, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh. He came to Jerusalem and tore down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

And he took the gold and the silver and all the vessels found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house. He also carried off the children of the foreigners, and he went back to Samaria.

And the rest of the acts of Jehoash, what he did by his might, and the battle he fought with Amaziah, king of Judah, are they not, behold, written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Jehoash slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. And Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.
And Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
And the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not, behold, written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And bands gathered against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. They followed him to Lachish and killed him there.
And they laid him on his horse and brought him back, and they buried him in Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David.
And all the people of Judah brought Azariah his son, who was only about eleven years old, and they made him king over them in place of his father.
He built Edom and rebuilt Judah after the death of his father.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned forty-one years.
And he did evil before the Lord and did not turn away from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray.

He restored the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath as far as the sea of Arabia, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which he spoke by the hand of his servant Jonah the prophet, son of Amittai, of Gath-hepher.
For the Lord saw the very bitter affliction of Israel: that they were diminished, distressed, in want and shut in, and there was no one to help Israel.
And the Lord did not want to blot out the race of Israel from under heaven, and he saved them by the hands of Jeroboam son of Joash.

And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and all his might with which he made war, and how he took Damascus and Hamath from Israel, are they not, behold, written in the books of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and Azariah son of Amaziah reigned in place of his father.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam, king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah, king of Judah, began to reign.
He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah, of Jerusalem.
And he did good before the Lord, just as his father Amaziah had done.
But he did not destroy the high places, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

And the Lord laid his hand on the king and poured leprosy upon him until the day of his death, and he lived in the house of Apphoth. And Jotham, the king's son, was over the house and judged the people of the land.
And the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the acts of the days of the kings of Judah?
And Azariah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David. And Jotham his son reigned in his place.
In the seventeenth[?] year of Azariah king of Judah, Azariah son of Jeroboam reigned in Samaria six months.
And he did evil before the Lord, as his fathers had done, and he did not turn away from the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray.
And Shallum and Kedebaam, the sons of Jabesh, rose up against him, and struck him before the people and killed him, and Shallum reigned in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Azariah, behold, are written in the books of the acts of the days of the kings of Israel.
This is the word of the Lord which he spoke to Jehu, saying: “Your descendants to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.” And so it came to pass.
And Shallum [?], the son of Jabesh, reigned in Samaria one month, in the twenty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah.
And Menahem son of Gadi came up from Tirzah and entered Samaria, and struck Shallum son of Jabesh and killed him, and he reigned in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he formed, behold, are written in the books of the acts of the days of the kings of Israel.
At that time Menahem struck Tirzah and all that was in it and all the territory of Tirzah, because they did not open the gate to him. And he destroyed them and ripped open their pregnant women.
In the thirty-third year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi reigned over Israel in Samaria ten years.
And he did evil before the Lord and did not turn away from all the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray by his sin.
And the king of Assyria came up against the land, and Menahem gave him as payment a thousand talents of silver, so that he would be his supporter and his kingship would be established by his hand.

Menahem exacted the silver from all Israel and from all the men of power who were able to give, and he gave the king of Assyria fifty talents of silver, from each man individually. And the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay in the land.
And the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, behold, are they not written in the books of the days of the acts of the kings of Israel?
And Menahem slept with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.
In the thirtieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah reigned over Israel in Samaria ten years.
And he did evil before the Lord and did not turn away from the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray.

And Pekah son of Remaliah, his own third officer, attacked him and struck him down in Samaria before the Lord, in the royal palace. And with him were Argob and Arieh and fifty men of the four hundred. And he killed him and reigned in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned twenty years.
And he did evil before the Lord, and did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray.

And in the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and took Ijon, Abel, Beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee and all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.
And Hoshea son of Elah formed a conspiracy and came against Pekah son of Remaliah, and struck him and killed him, and he reigned in his place in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
And the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the days of the kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah [?] king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah began to reign.
He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok.
And he did what was right before the Lord, according to all that his father Uzziah had done.
But he did not destroy the high places, and the people still burned incense and sacrificed on the high places. And he built the upper gates of the house of the Lord.

And the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah. In that time the Lord sent against Judah Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah.
And Jotham slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And Ahaz his son reigned in his place.
In the seventeenth year of the reign of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham began to reign.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And he did not do what was right before the Lord God, as David his father had done.

And he walked in the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, king of Israel; for he even made his own children pass through the flame of fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
And he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every shady tree.
At that time Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, came up against Jerusalem to make war. And they besieged it, but they were not able to [?take] Jerusalem.
At that time Rezin king of Syria seized Elath and drove the Jews out of Elath. And the Edomites came and settled in Elath, to this day.

And King Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of the Assyrians and said to him: "I am your servant and your son! Come up and save me from the hands of the king of the Assyrians and from the hands of the king of Israel, for they have risen up against me."
And he took the gold and silver that was found in the treasury of the house of the Lord and in the royal house, and sent it to the king of the Assyrians as a gift.
And the king of Assyria listened to him, and the king of Assyria went up against Damascus, captured it and carried it off captive, and they killed Kyrene [?] and Rezin.

And King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser, the king of the Assyrians. And Ahaz saw the altar that was in Damascus, and King Ahaz sent word to Urijah the priest, and sent him the measurements and showed him the pattern of its making.
And Urijah the priest made the altar.
And the king went up onto the altar.
And he offered his offerings and his pleasing sacrifices, and he poured out the blood of his peace offerings.
And as for the bronze altar that stood before the Lord, he moved it from its place and set it to one side of the altar, on the north side.

And King Ahaz commanded Urijah the priest, saying to him: "On this great altar offer the morning offerings and the evening offerings, and the king's offerings and his sacrifices, and the offerings of the people of the land and their sacrifices, and pour out on it all the blood of their sacrifices and of their slaughtered offerings; and the bronze altar shall be for me for [?]."
And Urijah the priest did in accordance with every command that King Ahaz had given him.
And King Ahaz cut off the panels of the stands and removed the basins from them, and he took the sea down from the twelve bronze oxen that were under it, and [?] it upon a stone pavement.
He built the foundation of the seat in the house of the Lord, and the king's going in and coming out of the house of the Lord was in peace because of the king of the Assyrians.
And the rest of the acts of Ahaz and whatever he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
And Ahaz slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, for nine years.
And he did evil before the Lord, but not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
And Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him, and Hoshea became his servant and brought him tribute.

And the king of Assyria found treachery in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to Adrammelech, the king of the Egyptians, and he did not give tribute to the king of the Assyrians that year. And the king of Assyria seized him and shut him up in prison.
And the king of Assyria went up through all the land, came also to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.

In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria captured Samaria and carried Israel away captive to Assyria, and settled them in Halah and Habor, on the rivers of Gozan, and in the mountains of the Medes.

And the wrath of the Lord was upon Israel, because the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had brought them up out of the land of the Egyptians, out of the hands of Pharaoh, and they feared other gods.
And they walked according to the ways of the nations whom the Lord had driven out before the children of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, in all that they did.

And the sons of Israel dressed up many words that were not right toward the Lord their God, and they built themselves high places in all their cities, from the watchmen's tower to the fortified cities.
And they set up pillars for worship on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
And they burned incense on all the high places, as all the nations had done whom the Lord had driven out before them. And they took partners, and they made [?] to provoke the Lord to anger.
And they served idols, about which the Lord had said to them: "Do not do this thing against the Lord."

And the Lord bore witness to the sons of Israel and to Judah through all the prophets and all the seers, and said to them: "Turn from your evil ways and keep my commandments and my ordinances and all the law that I commanded your fathers, which I sent to you through my servants the prophets."
But they did not listen to them. They hardened their backs more than their fathers had, and they did not believe the Lord their God.

And they rejected his covenant and everything he had established with their fathers, and they did not keep his testimony that he had commanded them. And they followed worthless things and became worthless, following the nations that were around them, whom the Lord had commanded them not to imitate.
And they abandoned all the commandments of the Lord their God and made themselves cast images, two heifers, and they bowed down to the hosts of heaven and served Baal.
And they passed their sons and their daughters through fire, and they practiced divination and cast spells, and they went on doing evil before the Lord to provoke him to anger.
And the Lord was angry with Israel and removed them from his presence, and no one was left except the tribe of Judah alone.
But Judah also did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God, and they walked in the ways of Israel, in what Israel had done.
And the whole race of Israel rejected the Lord, and he shook them and gave them into the hands of those who took them captive, until he had removed them from his presence.
And Israel broke away from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king over them. And Jeroboam led Israel away from the Lord and made them commit a great sin.
And the sons of Israel did all the sins that Jeroboam had done, and they did not turn away from them.
And the Lord removed Israel from his presence, as the Lord had said through all his servants the prophets. And Israel was carried away captive from its land to Assyria, where it is to this day.
And they settled in Samaria and took possession of its cities.
And at the beginning of their settlement there, they did not fear the Lord. So the Lord sent lions among them, and the lions were killing them.

They spoke to the king of Assyria and said: "The nations that you moved and settled in the cities do not know the law of the God of that land. So the Lord has sent lions among them, and the lions are killing them, because they do not know the law of the God of that land."
