And the king of Assyria commanded and said, "Take there one of the priests from among those taken captive from there, so that he may go and settle there and show them the law of the Lord, and teach them the ordinance of the God of that land."
So they took one of the priests who had been taken captive from Samaria, and he settled in Bethel and taught them how they should fear the Lord.
But each nation made its own gods and set them in the houses of the high places that the Samaritans had made, each nation in its own cities in which it had settled.
The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Senath [?],
and the Inaeans [?] made Ablazer [?] and Nibhaz and Tartak, and Sippharom [?], where they burned their sons with fire to Adrammelech and Amelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.

And they feared the Lord, and they set up their own abominations in the houses of the high places that they had made in Samaria, each nation where it had settled. And they feared the Lord and appointed for themselves priests of the high places.
And they feared the Lord, and they served their own gods according to the custom of the nations that God had destroyed.

And to this very day they act according to their custom. They fear the Lord, and they act according to their own pattern, and not according to the ordinance, the law and the commandment that the Lord gave to the sons of Jacob, whom he named Israel. [The Georgian lacks the "not"; it reads literally: "they act according to their own pattern and the ordinance, the law and the commandment..."]
The Lord made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, "Do not fear other gods, do not bow down to them, do not serve them and do not sacrifice to them,
but the Lord God, who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians with great power and an outstretched arm: fear him, bow down to him and sacrifice to him.
Be careful to keep the ordinance, the judgments, the laws and the commandments that he gave you, and do not fear their other gods.
Do not set aside the covenant that he made with you, and do not fear other gods,
but fear the Lord God, and he will deliver you from the hands of your enemies."
"And do not follow the pattern of what they do."
So these nations feared the Lord, and they served their carved images. Their children and their children's children do the same as their fathers did, to this very day.
In the second year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Abuth, daughter of Zechariah.
Hezekiah did what was right before the Lord, in every way as his father David had done.

He destroyed the high places, smashed all the pillars, cut down the groves, and destroyed the bronze serpents that Moses had made, because until that day the sons of Israel had been sacrificing to it. They called it by the name Iestana [?].
Hezekiah trusted in the Lord, the God of Israel. After him there was no one like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among all those who had been before him.
He held fast to the Lord and did not turn away from him, and he kept his commandments, which the Lord had given to Moses.
And the Lord was with him; in everything that he did, all went well for him. And King Hezekiah defied the king of the Assyrians and did not serve him.
And he struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and as far as their sea, from the watchmen's tower to their fortified [?] cities.
And it came to pass in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it.
And he took it in the third year. In the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Samaria was taken.
And the king of Assyria carried Samaria away captive to Assyria and settled them in Halah and Habor, by the rivers of Gozan, and in their mountains.
For they did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God and broke his covenant, everything that Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded them. They did not listen, and they did not do it.
In the twelfth year of the reign of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against the fortified cities of Judah and took them.

And the king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians at Lachish and said to him: "I have sinned. Withdraw from me, and whatever you lay on me I will bear." And the king of Assyria laid on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
And Hezekiah gave all the silver that was found in the house of the Lord and in the treasury of the king's house.
At that time Hezekiah cut down the doors of the temple of the Lord and the thresholds, which Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid with gold, and 200 [?] he gave it to the king of the Assyrians.

And the king of Assyria sent Tartan and Rabsaris and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a mighty army against Jerusalem. They set out, went up, came to Jerusalem, and stood by the conduit of the pool, which is on the road to the Fuller's Field.
And they called for Hezekiah, and there came out to them Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the steward of the household, and Shebna the chief scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder.
And Rabshakeh said to them: "Say to Hezekiah: Thus says the great king of Assyria: What is this confidence in which you trust?
Unless you said: 'But these are only words of the lips; counsel and strength are needed for war!' Now in whom do you trust, that you have defied me?
Behold, you trust in that staff of broken reed, Egypt, which, if a man leans on it, will pierce his hand and wound [?] it. So is Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, to all who trust in him.

And since you say to me, 'I trust in the Lord my God!', is this not that Hezekiah who removed the high places and tore down his altars, and said to Judah and Jerusalem, 'You shall worship before this altar in Jerusalem'?
Now come to terms with my lord the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses. Will you not find men to mount them?
How then can you stand against a single governor, the least of my lord's servants? And why do you trust in Egypt, in its chariots and horses?
And now, have we come up here to this place to destroy it without my lord? Rather, the Lord said to me: 'Go up against that land and destroy it.'"

Eliakim son of Hilkiah, and Shebna and Joah said to Rabshakeh: "Speak to your servants in the Assyrian tongue, and do not speak to us in the Judean tongue in the hearing of the people who are standing on the wall."
Rabshakeh said to them: "Was it to your lord, or to you, that he sent me to speak these words? Was it not to the men who are sitting on the walls, who will have to eat their own dung?"
Rabshakeh stood up and cried out with a loud voice in the Judean tongue. He spoke to them and said: "Hear the word of the great king of the Assyrians."
"Thus says the king: Do not let your king deceive [?] you, for he will not be able to deliver you from my hands.
"And do not let Hezekiah reassure you about the Lord by telling you: 'The Lord will surely deliver us, and he will not give this city into the hands of the king of Assyria.'

"Behold, do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree and drink water from his own cistern,

"until I come and take you away and bring you to a land like your own: a land of wheat and wine, of vineyards and bread, a land of oil, butter and honey. Then you will live and not die. And do not listen to Hezekiah, for he speaks to you and tells you: 'The Lord will deliver us.'
"Did the gods of the nations deliver each its own land from the hands of the king of Assyria?
"Where are the gods of Hamath and of Arpad? And where are the gods of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah? Did they deliver Samaria from my hands?
"Which of the gods of that country delivered their land from my hands? And will the Lord deliver Jerusalem from my hands?"
They answered him not a word, for the king had commanded: "Do not answer him a word."

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the steward of the household, Shebna the chief scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went in to Hezekiah with their garments torn and told him the words of Rabshakeh.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his garments, put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the Lord.
He sent Eliakim the steward of the household, Shebna the chief scribe, the elders of the priests, and the elders of the Jews, all clothed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz,
and they said to him: "Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of affliction and grief, of distress and groaning. The pains of women in labour have come, but they cannot give birth.

"May your God only hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom his lord the king of Assyria sent to revile the living God and to reproach him with words, which the Lord your God has heard. Pray for this remnant that is left."
So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah and told him this.
Isaiah said to them: "Say this to your lord: Thus says the Lord: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of the Assyrians reviled me.
"Behold, I will send an evil spirit upon him. He will hear a rumour [?] and return to his own land, and I will strike him down with the sword in his own land."
Rabshakeh went back and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had set out from Lachish.

And he heard about Tirhakah [?] the king of the Ethiopians, that: "Behold, he has come out to fight against you." And he went back to his own land [fol. 202r] and sent messengers to Hezekiah and said:
"Say this to Hezekiah, king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying: 'Jerusalem will not be given into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.'
Behold, you yourself have heard all that the kings of Assyria did to all the lands, how they plundered them. And do you now think that you will be delivered?
Did the gods of the nations that my fathers destroyed deliver them: Gozan and Haran and Rezeph and the sons of Edom [?] on the seashore?
Where is the god of Hamath? Where is the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ara [?]?"
And Hezekiah took the letter from the hands of the messengers and read it, and he went into the house of the Lord, and Hezekiah spread it out before the Lord.
And Hezekiah bowed down before the Lord and said: "O Lord, God of Israel, who sits upon the cherubim! You alone are over all the kings of the earth; you made heaven and earth.
Incline your ear, O Lord, and hear! Open your eyes, O Lord, and see, and hear the words of Sennacherib, which he sent to reproach the living God,
for truly, O, the kings of Assyria have destroyed those nations and their land.
And they gave their gods to the fire, for they were not gods at all, but the works of men's hands, of wood and of stone, and they destroyed them.
And now, O Lord our God, save us from his hands, so that all the kings of the earth may know that you alone are God."
And Isaiah son of Amoz sent to him and said: "Thus says the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel: I have heard what you prayed to me concerning Sennacherib.
This is the word which the Lord spoke concerning him: The virgin, the daughter of Zion, has despised and scorned you; the daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
Whom have you reviled and insulted? Against whom have you raised your voice in reproach and lifted up your eyes? Against the Holy One of Israel!

Through your messengers you have reproached the Lord and said: 'With the multitude of my chariots I have gone up to the heights of the mountains of Lebanon, and I have cut down the tall cypresses and the choicest pines, and I have reached the farthest end of the forest of Carmel.
I drank the water of the sea, and I dried up and trampled with the soles of my feet all the fierce rivers.'
Have you not heard long ago what I did to the former nations? I formed it from the beginning of days, and I have brought it to pass: and fortified cities have become plunder for warriors.

And those who dwelt [fol. 203r] in them grew weak of hand, and they trembled and were put to shame, and they became like the grass of the field and like the green herbage on a rooftop, to be trampled before those who came upon it.
Now I know your sitting down, your going out and your coming in, and your wrath,

with which you raged against me, and your arrogant clamor has reached my ears. And now I will put a hook in your nostrils and a bridle in your jaws, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.

And this shall be the sign for you: this year you shall eat what you have gathered, and in the second year you shall sow and eat what springs up from it, and in the third year you shall sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
And it shall be for that house of Judah: those who are left shall spread out their roots [?] and bear fruit,

for from Jerusalem a remnant shall go out, and from Mount Zion those who escape; for the zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this. Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians: He shall not enter that city, nor shoot arrows into it, nor surround it with shields, nor heap up earth against it.
By the way by which he came, by that he shall return, and he shall not enter that city, says the Lord.
And I will be a defender of that city, to save it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.

And it came to pass that on that night the angel of the Lord went out and struck down one hundred and eighty-five thousand men from the camp of the Assyrians. And they rose early in the morning, and behold, they saw all those many dead bodies.
And the king of Assyria turned back and went away, and settled in Nineveh.

And it came to pass, while he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch, his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, struck him down with the sword, and they fled to the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

In those days Hezekiah fell sick with a mortal illness. And the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came in to him and said to him: Thus says the Lord: Set your house in order, for you shall die and shall not escape.
And Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord and said:
O Lord, remember that I have walked before you in truth and with a whole heart, and I have done what is pleasing to you. And Hezekiah wept with great weeping.
And Isaiah was in the great court, and the word of the Lord came to him and said:

Turn back there and say to Hezekiah, the leader of my people: Thus says the Lord, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer and I have seen your tears; [fol. 204r] behold, I will heal you, and on the third day you shall go up to the house of the Lord.

And I will add fifteen years to your days, and I will deliver you from the hands of the king of the Assyrians; and I will be a defender of this city for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.
Isaiah said: Take figs and oil and lay them on the wound, and he will recover.
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah: What will be the sign that the Lord will heal me, and that I shall go up to the house of the Lord on the third day?
And Isaiah said: This shall be the sign from the Lord that the Lord will do the thing that he has spoken: the shadow shall go down ten steps.
And Hezekiah said: It is easy for the shadow to go down ten steps. Not so; rather, let it turn back the same ten steps.
And the prophet Isaiah cried out to the Lord, and the shadow turned back those same ten steps by which it had come down on the buildings of Ahaz.
At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan sent envoys with [?] and gifts to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had fallen ill. And he arose

And Hezekiah rejoiced at their coming, and he showed them all his treasure houses: the silver and the gold, the incense and the ointments, the storehouses, and whatever was found in his treasury. There was nothing in his house, of all his dominion, that Hezekiah did not show them.
And Isaiah the prophet came in and said to him: "What did those men say to you, and where did they come to you from?" And Hezekiah said: "They came to me from a far country, from Babylon."
And he said: "What did they see in your house?" Hezekiah said to him: "They saw everything that was in my house. There was nothing that I did not show them, my treasures as well."
And Isaiah said to Hezekiah: "Hear the word of the Lord!

Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when they will carry off everything that is in your house. What your fathers have stored up until this day they will carry off to Babylon, and they will leave nothing, for this is the word that the Lord has spoken.
And they will also take away some of your offspring, and they will make them eunuchs in the house of the king of the Babylonians."
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah: "The word that you have spoken is good. Let there be peace and truth in my days."

And the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, all his mighty deeds, the water conduits and the tunnels that he made, and the waters that he brought into the city, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and Manasseh his son [205r] reigned in his place.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hephzibah.
And Manasseh did evil before the Lord, following the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had wiped out before the sons of Israel.

And he rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built the altars of Baal and set up the groves, as Ahab king of Israel had set them up, and he worshipped all the host of heaven and served them.
And he built an altar in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord had said: "In Jerusalem I will set up my throne."
And he made places of worship for all the host of heaven in all the courts of the house of the Lord.

And he made his children pass through fire. He practised sorcery and divination, he appointed mediums and multiplied soothsayers, and he did more and more evil before the Lord, provoking him to anger.

And he set up the carved image of the groves in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord had said to David and to his son Solomon: "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.

And I will no longer make the feet of Israel be moved from that land which I gave to their fathers, if only they take care to do everything that I have commanded them, according to all the commandment that my servant Moses commanded them."

But they did not listen. Manasseh became exceedingly abominable, and he led them astray to do evil before the Lord, more than all the nations that the Lord had destroyed before the face of the sons of Israel.
The Lord spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets:
And he said this because Manasseh, king of Judah, did these abominations and wickedness, more than the Amorite before me, and led Judah astray with his idols.
Therefore thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Behold, I will bring evil upon Jerusalem and upon Judah, so that both ears of all who hear of it will ring.
And I will stretch over Jerusalem the measure of Samaria and the balance of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe Jerusalem out as a dish is emptied and turned upside down.
And I will cast off the remnant of my inheritance and give them into the hands of their enemies, and they shall become plunder and spoil for all their enemies,
because they turned away from my face and did evil before my eyes and provoked me to anger from the day I brought them out of the land of the Egyptians until this day.
And Manasseh also shed a very great deal of innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem from end to end, besides his own sin, by which he led Judah astray into doing evil before the Lord.
And the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and all that he did, and the sin that he sinned, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
And Manasseh slept with his fathers and was buried in his garden, the garden of Uzziah, and Amon his son reigned in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Meshullemeth, daughter of Haruz, from Jotbah.
And Amon did evil before the Lord, as Manasseh his father had done.
And he walked in all the ways in which his father had walked, and served the idols that his father had served, and bowed down to them.
And he forsook the God of his fathers and did not walk in the ways of the Lord.
And his servants rose up against him and killed him in his own house.
And the people struck down those who had killed Amon, and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Amon, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
And Amon slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the garden of Uzziah. And Josiah his son reigned in his place.
Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-eight [?] years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jedidah, daughter of Uzziah, from Bozkath.
And Josiah did what was right before the Lord and walked in all the ways of David his father, and he turned aside neither to the right nor to the left.
And in the eighteenth year of Josiah king of Judah, in the seventh month, the king sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the scribe of the house of the Lord, and said to him:

Go to Hilkiah the high priest and tell him to melt down together the silver that has been brought as an offering into the house of the Lord, which the keepers of the balance have collected from the people.

And let them give it into the hands of those doing the work, the overseers of the house of the Lord. And let them give it to the workers of the house of the Lord, so that they may repair the breach of the house of the Lord:
to the carpenters and builders and craftsmen, to buy timber and stones for repairing the breach of the house of the Lord.
And they did not weigh out to them the silver that they gave to the workmen, because they worked faithfully.
And Hilkiah, the high priest, said to Shaphan the chief scribe: "I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord." And Hilkiah gave it to Shaphan
and Shaphan read it before the king.
When the king heard the words of the book, he tore his clothes.
And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Achbor son of Micaiah, and Shaphan the chief scribe, and Azariah the king's servant, and said to them:

"Go and inquire of the Lord for me, and for all this people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that has been found; for great is the wrath of the Lord that is kindled against us, because our fathers did not listen and did not obey the words of this book, according to all that is written for us."

And Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam, and Shaphan, and Achbor, and Azariah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Adrai, the keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem, in the Mishneh. And they spoke to her.
And she said to them: "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Tell the man who sent you to me:
Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring evil upon this place and upon its inhabitants, according to all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read,

because they have forsaken me and burned incense to foreign gods, so as to provoke me to anger with the works of their hands; and my wrath has been kindled [?] against this place and will not be quenched.
And now go back to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the Lord, and say this to him: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: The words that you have heard

are concerning them; but because your heart was softened and you humbled yourself before the Lord when you heard what was spoken against this place and against its inhabitants, that they would become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your clothes and wept before me, I too have heard you, says the Lord.

Not so; rather, I will gather you to your fathers, and you will go to your grave in peace in Jerusalem, and your eyes will not see all the evil that I will bring upon this place and upon its inhabitants."
And they reported this word to the king. And the king gathered all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem.

And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and with him every man of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the priests, and all the prophets, and all the people with him, from the least to the greatest. And he read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of the Lord.

And the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord to follow after the Lord and to keep his commandments and his ordinances with all his heart, to perform the words of this covenant that had been found in the book. And all the people stood to the covenant.

And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second rank, and the keepers of the balance, to bring out of the house of the Lord all the vessels made for Baal, for the groves and for the host of heaven. And he burned them outside Jerusalem, in the fields [?] of the Kidron, and scattered their ashes at Bethel.

And he also burned the pagan priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed, who [fol. 208r] burned incense on the high places and in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, and those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, to the moon, to the stars and to all the host of heaven.

And he brought the grove out of the house of the Lord [?] to the brook of the Kidron outside Jerusalem. He burned them with fire in the brook of the Kidron, ground them fine as dust, and scattered their ashes on the grave of the sons of the people.
And he pulled down the house of the cult prostitutes (kadeshim), which was beside the house of the Lord, where the women wove garments for the groves.

And he drove out all the pagan priests from the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba. And he pulled down the houses by the gates of Eli, the ruler of the city, on the left side of the gates.
But the priests of the high places did not go up to the altar in Jerusalem, except to eat unleavened bread among their brothers.
Then he defiled Tophet in the valley of the son of Hinnom, so that no one would make his sons and daughters pass through the fire of Molech.

And they burned the horses that the king of Judah had dedicated in the name of the sun at the entrance of the house of the Lord, by the chamber of Nathan the eunuch, which was in Parurim. He burned with fire the chariots dedicated in the name of the sun.

And the altars that were on the roof, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord: the king pulled them down, smashed them, and threw their dust into the brook of the Kidron.

And the house that stood facing Jerusalem, on the right side of the mount of Mosoth [?], which Solomon king of Israel had built for Astarte, the abomination of the Sidonians, for Chemosh, the abomination of the Moabites, and for Molech, the horror of the sons of Ammon, he also defiled.
And the king smashed the pillars, cut down the groves, and filled their places with human bones.

And the high altars that were at Bethel, which Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray, had made: that high altar too he overthrew. He smashed its stones, ground them fine as dust, and burned the grove.

And Josiah turned and saw the tombs that were in the city. He sent and had the bones taken out of the tombs, burned them on the altars, and defiled the altars, according to the word of the Lord that the man of God, while he was still alive, had spoken to Jeroboam at the sacrifice on the altar. He turned toward the tomb [fol. 209r] of the man of God who had spoken the word ...
And he said: "What is that place which [?] [I see]?" The men of that place said to him: "It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these words against the altar at Bethel."

And Josiah said: "Let it be, and do not disturb his bones!" So the bones of the old prophet who had lived in Bethel were spared, along with the bones of the man of God who had come from Judah; he had foretold all these things that Josiah did.

And Josiah, king of Judah, tore down all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, and he did to them just as had been done at Bethel.
And he slaughtered all the priests of the high places on the altars and burned their bones on them, and he returned to Jerusalem.
And the king commanded, saying: "Keep the feast of the Lord our God, as it is written in the book of the covenant!"
And they did so. No feast like that feast had been kept since the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor in the days of the kings of Israel and of Judah.
And in the eighteenth year of King Josiah the Passover of the Lord was kept in Jerusalem.

And King Josiah also did away with the mediums [?], the diviners, the teraphim, the idols, and all the abominations that were in Judah and in Jerusalem, in order to carry out the words of the law that were written in the book which Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the Lord.
None of the kings before him was like him, turning to the Lord with all his heart, all his soul, and all his strength, according to all the law of Moses; and after him there was none like him.
Yet the Lord did not turn back from his anger and his great wrath, which burned against Judah because of all the provocations by which Manasseh had provoked him.
And the Lord said: "I will remove Judah also from my presence, as I removed Israel. And I will reject this city of Jerusalem, which I chose, and the temple of which I said, 'My name shall be there.'"
And the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
In his days Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, went up against the king of Assyria, to the river [?] Euphrates. And King Josiah went out to meet him, and Pharaoh killed him at Megiddo when he met him.

And his servants carried him from Megiddo, brought him back to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb in the city of David. [fol. 210r] And the people of the land took Jehoahaz, son of Josiah, and made him king over them.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
And Jehoahaz did evil in the sight of the Lord, just as his fathers had done.

And Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, removed him at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that he would no longer reign in Jerusalem, and he imposed on the land a tribute of a hundred talents of silver and ten talents of gold.

And Pharaoh Necho set Eliakim [?], son of Josiah, as king over them, as king over Judah in place of Josiah his father, and gave him the name Jehoiakim. And he took Jehoahaz away to Egypt, and he died there.

And Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh. But the land was taxed harshly to give the silver to Pharaoh: the silver and gold of the people of the land were taken from each man for Pharaoh Necho.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twelve years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Eldaph, daughter of Iedala, from Rumah.
And he did evil before the Lord, just as his fathers had done in everything.
In his days Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came up, and Jehoiakim served him for three years. Then he turned and broke faith with him.

And the Lord sent raiding bands against Jehoiakim: raiders from Chaldea, raiders from Assyria, raiders from Moab and raiders of the sons of Ammon. He sent them against the land of Judea to destroy them, according to the word of the Lord that he had spoken by the hand of his servants the prophets.
For the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah, to remove them from his presence for the sins of Manasseh, which he committed,
and for the innocent blood that they shed, filling Jerusalem with that innocent blood. And the Lord was not willing to pardon them.
And the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and everything he did, behold, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and Jehoiachin reigned in his place.

And the king of Egypt did not come out of his land again, for the king of Babylon had taken everything from the Brook of Egypt as far as the river Euphrates, everything that had belonged to the king of the Egyptians.
Jehoiachin was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Esta, daughter of Ielamath, from Jerusalem.
And he did evil before the Lord, just as his fathers had done in everything. [fol. 211r]
At that time the king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem and surrounded the city.
And the king of the Babylonians came to the city, while his servants were besieging it on every side.

And Jehoiachin, king of Judah, went out to the king of Babylon: he himself and all his servants, his mother, his princes and his eunuchs. And the king of Babylon took them away in the eighth year of his reign.

And he carried off all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house. He cut up all the gold vessels that Solomon, king of Israel, had made in the temple of the Lord, according to the word of the Lord.
And he carried away all Jerusalem: all the princes, all the mighty men of valor, a thousand captives, all the craftsmen and all the guards. No one was left there except the poor of the land.
And he carried Jehoiachin away to Babylon, along with the king's mother, his wives, his eunuchs and the mighty men of the land, and they went into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
And all the men of might, seven thousand men, and the craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand men, all of them mighty men and warriors: the king of the Babylonians carried them off captive to Babylon.
And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, his son, king in his place, and gave him the name Zedekiah.
When he was made king, he also reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, of Libnah.
And he did evil before the Lord, just as Jehoiakim had done in everything.
For the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah and upon Jerusalem, until he cast them out from his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

And in the ninth year of his reign, in the ninth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came against Jerusalem with all his army. He encamped against Jerusalem and built a siege wall all around it.
And the city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah,
until the ninth month. And the famine grew severe in the city, and the people of the city had no food.

And the city was overcome, and the king and all the people went out by night by way of the gate between the walls, by the royal garden. The Chaldeans were surrounding the city, and they went off by the road to Arabia.
And the whole army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him at Aramoth of Jericho, and all his people scattered from him.
And they seized the king and brought him before the king of the Babylonians at Riblah, and he pronounced judgment on him.
And he slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, [fol. 212r] and he put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him in fetters and carried him off to Babylon.

And in the fifth month, on the fifth day of the month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, Nebuzaradan, the chief of the cooks, who served before the king of the Babylonians, came to Jerusalem.
And he burned the house of the Lord and the royal palace, and he burned all the houses of Jerusalem with fire.
And the walls of Jerusalem were torn down by the whole army of the Chaldeans who were with the chief of the cooks.

And the mighty men of the people who were left in the city, those who had deserted to the king of the Babylonians, and the rest of the multitude of the people, Nebuzaradan the cook carried off captive.
And Nebuzaradan left the peasants of the land to be vinedressers and treasurers [?].

And the two bronze pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the stands, and the mechonoth [?], and the bronze sea that was in the house of the Lord, the Chaldeans broke in pieces, and they carried the bronze off to Babylon.
And the cauldrons [?], the shovels [?], the basins, the bowls, the [?] and all the vessels used in the service, he carried these off too.
Nebuzaradan also carried off the firepans [?] and the bowls [?] of gold and of silver.
And the two pillars, the one sea and the mechonoth that Solomon had made for the house of the Lord: there was no weighing the bronze of them and of all the vessels that Nebuzaradan carried off.

Each pillar was eighteen cubits high, with a bronze capital on top of it. Each capital was three cubits high. All around the capital were a network and pomegranate shapes, all of bronze. The head of the second pillar had the same form.
Nebuzaradan took away Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the scales.

From the city he took one eunuch, who was in charge of the fighting men, and five men who stood before the king and were found in the city. He also took the chief scribe of the commander of the army, the one who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
Nebuzaradan the chief cook took them away and brought them to the king of the Babylonians at Riblah.
The king of the Babylonians put them to death at Riblah, in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away captive from its own land.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon left behind the people of Judah who remained, and he set over them Gedaliah, son of Ahikam son of Shaphan.

All the commanders of the land heard that the king of Babylon had set Gedaliah over them at Mizpah. These were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Nathan the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite: those chiefs, together with their men.

Those chiefs and their men swore an oath to Gedaliah. Gedaliah said to them: "Do not be afraid of the [?] of the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of the Babylonians, and it will go well with you."

In the eighth month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, who was of royal descent, came with ten men. They struck Gedaliah and killed him. They also killed the Jews and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
Then all the people, from the least to the greatest, rose up together with the commanders of the army and went down to Egypt, because they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

In the seventeenth year after Jehoiachin king of Judah was taken captive, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, in the first year of the reign of Merodach, Merodach king of Babylon raised up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of the prison house.
He spoke kindly to him and placed his throne above those of all the others who sat enthroned with the king in Babylon.
He took off his prison clothes, and for the rest of his life Jehoiachin ate his meals in the king's presence.
For the rest of his life he was given a regular allowance from the royal house every day.
